subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold it into the broader Control UI notification architecture, or leave shell-originated alerts to plugin/external delivery paths until a generic notification API exists?
rationale: The feature is absent and useful, but it defines a new admin-facing Gateway/UI interruption path with security, product, and overlap decisions that automation should not settle.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Notification Architecture
options.body: Make the broader Control UI notification tracker own the in-app toast/action contract, and keep this issue linked for the shell/admin broadcast requirement.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a core command for now and document the supported plugin, Web Push, channel, or node-notification path once maintainers choose that boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the best available routing owner from current history and prior review context across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI notification boundaries.
